name: usermod
description: Modifies an existing user account: groups, shell, home directory, lock state, and more.

flags.description: Append the user to additional groups (-a is critical — without it, -G replaces all group memberships).
Move the home directory to PATH along with its contents.
Rename the user (does not rename the home directory by itself).

examples.explanation: Grants alice sudo (administrator) rights by adding her to the sudo group. THE most common usermod command.
Allows alice to use Docker without sudo. She must log out and back in for group changes to take effect.
Disables interactive login for an account while keeping it for services.
Locks the account by prefixing the password hash in /etc/shadow with !. Unlock with -U.

about: usermod applies the same underlying changes as useradd but to existing accounts. The -aG idiom is essential: usermod -G docker alice (without -a) would remove alice from every other group — a classic way to accidentally revoke sudo access from an admin account.
useCases: Temporarily lock accounts instead of deleting them.
mistakes: Forgetting -a in -aG and wiping out all other group memberships.
Changing your own shell to something that does not exist and being unable to log in.
warnings: Group changes require a new login session. If you lock or change the shell of the only admin account over SSH, keep your current session open until you have verified a second one works.
